memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Do not blaspheme God or curse the ruler of your people." - Exodus 22:28 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God calls His people to honour both Himself and the leaders He has placed over them. To blaspheme God is to speak against the One who is worthy of all reverence. To curse those in authority is to tear at the order God has established for a peaceful society. Our words toward God and toward those over us reveal much about the reverence in our hearts.

This is a searching command in an age where mocking God and tearing down leaders have almost become sport. It is easy to join the loud chorus of contempt, to speak carelessly about sacred things, to pour scorn on every authority we dislike. But God calls His people to a different spirit — one marked by reverence for Him and respect for the offices He allows to exist, even when we disagree with those who hold them.

This does not mean we cannot lament injustice or speak truth to power; Scripture is full of bold, honest voices. But there is a difference between honest challenge and corrosive contempt. The New Testament echoes this call, urging us to honour rulers and to pray for those in authority rather than merely revile them (1 Pet 2:17; 1 Tim 2:1-2). May our words, even in disagreement, carry the fragrance of a heart that reveres God and respects the order He has built.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Do my words about God and about leaders reflect reverence and respect?
How can I speak honestly about wrongs without falling into corrosive contempt?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, guard my tongue from irreverence toward You and contempt toward others. Let my words carry respect even in disagreement, honouring the order You have established. Amen.
